attribution.detail: torch.profiler CPU/CUDA activities profile only objective backward; bounded top-30 self/inclusive key averages, total event counts and microsecond units. Profiled backward wall overhead is 25.901x/24.580x control, so instrumented latency is diagnostic only. Module attribution is unassigned; top keys are generic ATen/profiler labels; no GDN/attention/expert percentages or speedup claim.

environment.detail: Clean pinned source 6e891166 and instruction 2babd43; RTX 4090/driver 580.178.04, 24,077 MiB free; Python 3.12.7/torch 2.10.0+cu128/CUDA 12.8; 26.1 GB host RAM and 182 GB scratch available; deterministic/TF32 off; BF16 only; FP8 reuse disabled.

exactness.detail: Four fresh-process BF16 cases: T512 control/profile and T2048 control/profile. Losses, full gradient inventory/digest, post-update model digest, optimizer-state digest and identity are exactly equal per length; accepted T0020 BF16 identity and exact pre-update losses match at both lengths. All 43,055,076 parameters and gradients FP32/finite; no missing gradients.

handover.detail: Flat attempt package with sanitized driver/comparator, four case JSONs, equality files, bounded attribution aggregates, environment, metrics, execution log and summary; validator result reported in PR body.

limitations: Four single-update BF16 cases; no steady-state, convergence, quality or production-throughput claim.
torch.profiler adds severe perturbation; instrumented latency is diagnostic only, not a speed measurement.
Only bounded top-30 key averages per axis are published; no full traces and no complete event attribution.
Self CPU/device times overlap and are not additive; module attribution remains unassigned from generic ATen/profiler keys.
No GDN, attention, expert or optimizer module percentages are inferred; a scoped instrumentation IMP is proposed.
No real data, checkpoint, Mini, package, kernel or reference-source change.
